dot_guide.intro: América is turning 250 years old — a quarter millennium of history, invention, and adventure! What better way to celebrate than soaring above the festivities in a magnificent balão a gás? Gas balões were one of the very first flying machines, and Americans have loved them since the earliest days of the republic. Pegue um lápis, encontre o ponto 1 e let's send this balloon up into the celebration sky!

sections.title: O envelope do balão
sections.learn: Start at ponto 1 and ligue through to ponto 10 to trace the large, rounded top of the balloon envelope — the big colourful bag that holds the gas and gives the balloon its classic shape. Children practise wide, sweeping curves here, which are wonderful for building smooth controle do lápis and wrist flexibility.
sections.fact: Gas balões are filled with lighter-than-air gas, often helium today, which makes the envelope buoyant enough to lift the basket. The envelope can hold thousands of cubic feet of gas, and its round shape helps spread pressure evenly in all directions.

sections.title: O detalhe das estrelas e listras
sections.learn: Continue from ponto 11 to ponto 22 to add the decorative panel lines and patriotic details that wrap around the balloon. Balloon envelopes are typically made from many separate panels sewn together, and these seam lines create the beautiful geometric patterns you see in the finished picture. Children practise shorter, more directional strokes here.
sections.fact: Early americano balloonists sometimes decorated their balões with patriotic colours and symbols to celebrate the new nation. The Flag Act of 1818 set the modern rule of 13 stripes, with one star for each state. That is why the Stars and Stripes could keep growing as new states joined the Estados Unidos.

sections.title: A rede e o anel de carga
sections.learn: Trace pontos 23 through 34 to draw the netting that wraps around the outside of the balloon and the load ring — the circular hoop at the very bottom of the envelope where the basket hangs. Children practise a network of crisscrossing lines, which is a brilliant exercise in precision and planning ahead.
sections.fact: The rope netting around many gas balões is not just decorative — it helps spread the weight of the basket and passengers across the balloon envelope. Sharing the weight over many ropes helps the balloon stay balanced and strong.

sections.title: As cordas de suspensão e a cesta
sections.learn: Ligue pontos 35 to 42 to draw the suspension ropes trailing down from the load ring and the wicker basket hanging at the bottom. The basket — called a gondola — is where the pilot and passengers stand. Children practise parallel lines converging to a single shape, which builds wonderful spatial reasoning skills.
sections.fact: As cestas de balões são feitas de vime há mais de 200 anos, e o vime ainda é um material favorito hoje. O vime é leve e flexível, por isso pode dobrar um pouco suavemente durante o pouso. Às vezes, os métodos antigos são realmente os melhores!

sections.title: A bandeira e os toques finais
sections.learn: Finish the atividade by connecting pontos 43 through 48 to add the americano flag and the final celebratory details. Just six pontos to bring the whole scene together — encourage crianças to slow down and make these last lines their best. A clean, confident finish is the sign of a true ponto-to-ponto expert!
sections.fact: América's first balloon pilot was Jean-Pierre Blanchard, a Frenchman who made his historic flight from Philadelphia on 9 January 1793. President George Washington gave him a letter of safe passage to present to anyone he met after landing — which turned out to be very useful, as he came down in a farm field in New Jersey and needed to explain who he was!

dot_guide.outro: Ótimo trabalho! O seu balão comemorativo dos 250 anos da América está pronto para voar! São 48 pontos e um céu cheio de celebração. Pinte-o de vermelho, branco e azul para celebrar o incrível 250º aniversário dos Estados Unidos. Feliz aniversário, EUA! Perfeito para a sala de aula — veja mais atividades de ligar os pontos .

dot_guide.intro: América is celebrating its 250th aniversário, and the nation's most iconic symbol — the bald águia — is here to lead the festivities! With a patriotic faixa streaming behind it, this majestic bird soars high over the celebration. Eagles have stood for americano freedom and strength since the very earliest days of the republic. Grab your pencil, find ponto 1, and let's send this águia soaring!

sections.title: A cabeça e o bico da águia
sections.learn: Start at ponto 1 and ligue through to ponto 16 to trace the águia's bold white head and sharp, curved beak. These carefully directed strokes help crianças warm up their pencil grip and build the confident hand control they'll need for the wings ahead. Encourage them to draw slowly and aim for each ponto precisely.
sections.fact: As águias americanas não são realmente carecas - seu nome vem de uma antiga palavra inglesa "balde", que significa branco. As impressionantes penas brancas da cabeça aparecem quando a ave atinge a idade adulta, por volta dos cinco anos de idade. Antes disso, as águias jovens tinham plumagem manchada de marrom e branco, o que as torna muito mais difíceis de reconhecer.

sections.title: As asas estendidas
sections.learn: Continue from ponto 17 to ponto 36 to draw the águia's powerful, outstretched wings — the most dramatic part of the picture. These long, sweeping strokes from wingtip to body are a wonderful exercise for wrist flexibility and smooth line control. Children practise holding a consistent direction across a larger stretch of the page.
sections.fact: A bald águia's wingspan can reach up to 2.4 metres — almost eight feet from tip to tip — making it one of the largest birds of prey in North América. Those massive wings allow eagles to soar on thermal currents of warm rising air for hours without a single wingbeat, covering enormous distances with very little effort.

sections.title: As penas e garras da cauda
sections.learn: Trace pontos 37 through 54 to add the fan of white tail feathers and the powerful curved talons below. Children practise a mix of fanning strokes for the feathers and sharp, precise curves for each talon — a great combination for building both fluency and control in a single section.
sections.fact: An águia's talons are its primary hunting tool, capable of gripping with a force of around 400 pounds per square inch — many times stronger than a human hand. The bald águia also has a specially rough, spiky texture on the soles of its feet called spicules, which help it grip slippery fish pulled straight from rivers and lakes.

sections.title: A Bandeira Patriótica
sections.learn: Ligue pontos 55 through 68 to draw the flowing faixa that streams behind the águia. The ribbon-like curves of a faixa in motion are a brilliant challenge for smooth, flowing line work. Encourage crianças to imagine the faixa fluttering in a summer breeze as they draw each gentle arc.
sections.fact: The bald águia holds a faixa or ribbon in its beak on many famous americano emblems and seals. On the Great Seal of the Estados Unidos, the águia holds a ribbon reading "E Pluribus Unum" — Latin for "Out of Many, One" — a motto that has appeared on americano coins and documents since 1782.

sections.title: As estrelas e os toques finais
sections.learn: Finish the atividade by connecting pontos 69 through 80 to add the patriotic estrelas and the final celebratory details that bring the whole scene to life. Just twelve pontos to complete the picture — encourage crianças to slow down and make these last lines their very best. A clean, careful finish is the mark of a true ponto-to-ponto champion!
sections.fact: The 50 estrelas on the americano flag each represent one of the 50 states in the union. The flag has been updated 27 times as new states joined — the most recent change came in 1960, when Hawaii's star was added. The current 50-star design has now been the official flag for longer than any other version in americano history.

dot_guide.intro: América is turning 250 years old — and what better way to mark a quarter millennium than with a sky full of dazzling fogos de artifício? Fireworks have lit up the Fourth of July since the very earliest days of the nation, turning the night sky into a canvas of colour and light. Grab your pencil, find ponto 1, and let's set off this spectacular aniversário display!

sections.title: O céu noturno
sections.learn: Start at ponto 1 and ligue through to ponto 18 to trace the deep, starry sky that forms the backdrop of the display. These wide sweeping strokes help crianças warm up their pencil grip and build the smooth, confident lines they'll need for the exciting fogos de artifício bursts ahead.
sections.fact: The night sky looks dark because the sun is on the other side of the Earth, but it is never truly empty — on a clear night away from city lights, you can see up to 4,500 estrelas with the naked eye. That same sky greeted the Founding Fathers when they first celebrated independence in 1776.

sections.title: A primeira explosão de fogos de artifício
sections.learn: Continue from ponto 19 to ponto 36 to draw the first big firework explosion bursting open in the sky. Children practise radiating lines that shoot outward from a central point — a wonderful exercise for directional control and wrist rotation.
sections.fact: Os fogos de artifício foram inventados na China há mais de 1.000 anos, quando os alquimistas descobriram que uma mistura de carvão, enxofre e nitrato de potássio produziria um clarão e um estrondo brilhantes. A receita finalmente chegou à Europa e depois às Américas, onde se tornou o som característico da celebração.

sections.title: As faíscas em cascata
sections.learn: Trace pontos 37 through 54 to add the glittering cascade of sparks that trail downward after the main burst. These curving, falling lines give the fogos de artifício their signature weeping-willow shape and offer great practice in drawing smooth, gentle curves.
sections.fact: The different colours in fogos de artifício come from burning different metal salts: strontium salts produce red, barium salts make green, copper compounds create blue, and sodium compounds give off bright yellow. Mixing these salts lets pyrotechnicians paint the sky with almost any colour they choose.

sections.title: A explosão do Grand Finale
sections.learn: Ligue pontos 55 through 72 to reveal the biggest and brightest firework of all — the grand finale explosion that fills the centre of the sky. Children practise a dense starburst of lines converging at a single point, which is a brilliant challenge for precision and spatial planning.
sections.fact: The "grand finale" tradition in fogos de artifício displays came about because early professional pyrotechnicians wanted to end shows with maximum impact before the crowd could disperse. Today's grand finales can fire hundreds of shells per minute, turning the sky almost as bright as daylight for a thrilling few seconds.

sections.title: As estrelas, a bandeira e os toques finais
sections.learn: Finish the atividade by connecting pontos 73 through 90 to add the patriotic estrelas, the waving americano flag, and the final celebratory details that complete the aniversário scene. Encourage crianças to take their time — these last pontos bring the whole picture to life. A careful, confident finish is the mark of a true ponto-to-ponto champion!
sections.fact: The americano flag has 50 estrelas — one for each state — and 13 stripes representing the original colonies. On the Fourth of July each year, the flag is flown from sunrise to sunset at homes, schools, and government buildings across the country, from the smallest town to the White House.

dot_guide.intro: América is turning 250 years old — and what better symbol to celebrate than the Sino da Liberdade! This legendary State House bell hung in Philadelphia when the Declaration of Independence was adopted, and its message of liberty became famous in the 1800s. Grab your pencil, find ponto 1, and let's make freedom ring!

sections.fact: The Sino da Liberdade's wooden yoke is made from americano elm, though historians cannot prove it is the bell's original yoke. The bell was hung from a wooden support so it could swing freely and produce its deep, resonant tone across colonial Philadelphia.

sections.fact: The Sino da Liberdade weighs 2,080 pounds — nearly a tonne! It was cast from a mix of copper and tin, which is the traditional recipe for bronze. The bell's distinctive deep tone comes from its large size and the precise ratio of metals used in its construction.

sections.title: As asas crescentes
sections.learn: Trace pontos 27 through 39 to add the magnificent wings that lift the Sino da Liberdade towards the sky. These bold, sweeping arcs give crianças a wonderful opportunity to practise long, flowing lines — building the arm movement and directional control that are key early writing skills.
sections.fact: The bald águia — symbol of the Estados Unidos since 1782 — is famous for its enormous wingspan of up to 2.4 metres (8 feet). Its powerful wings allow it to soar on warm air currents called thermals, reaching speeds of 45 miles per hour in level flight and even faster when diving.

sections.title: As estrelas e os detalhes patrióticos

These shorter, more precise lines are great for building fine motor control — crianças must foco carefully to hit each ponto accurately, which sharpens the hand–eye coordination needed for reading and writing.
sections.fact: The 50 estrelas on the americano flag each represent one of the 50 states. The first official Stars and Stripes design was approved in 1777 with 13 estrelas and 13 stripes for the original states. New estrelas have been added as new states joined the Union, with the most recent — Hawaii — added on 4 July 1960.

sections.fact: 1776 is one of the most important years in americano history. On 4 July 1776, the Continental Congress formally adopted the Declaration of Independence, proclaiming that all thirteen americano colonies were grátis and independent states. That date is now celebrated every year as Independence Day — América's aniversário.

sections.fact: A hélice de um avião com motor a pistão funciona como uma asa giratória – cada pá é moldada de modo que girá-la no ar gere impulso para frente. As primeiras hélices de madeira eram esculpidas à mão em curvas exatas, e artesãos habilidosos podiam moldar uma hélice que combinasse perfeitamente com a potência de um motor específico.

sections.fact: Os primeiros aviões tinham cabines abertas sem pára-brisas – os pilotos usavam capacetes de couro, óculos de proteção e cachecóis para se protegerem do vento e do frio em altitude. Cockpits fechados com cobertura de vidro só se tornaram padrão na maioria dos aviões na década de 1930, tornando o voo muito mais confortável.

sections.title: As asas

Encourage crianças to aim for each ponto calmly and let the pencil glide — just like a plane riding a current of smooth air.
sections.fact: An aeroplane's wings generate lift because of their curved upper surface and flatter underside. Air moving over the curved top travels faster and creates lower pressure, enquanto slower air beneath pushes up — and together, this pressure difference lifts the entire aircraft off the ground.

sections.fact: A barbatana caudal – também chamada de estabilizador vertical – mantém o avião apontando para frente, assim como os vôos de uma flecha. Sem ele, o nariz balançaria para a esquerda e para a direita incontrolavelmente à mais leve brisa. Os estabilizadores horizontais menores acima e abaixo dele controlam a inclinação para cima e para baixo da aeronave.

sections.fact: Aerial faixa towing began in the Estados Unidos in the 1920s, when clever pilots realised they could earn extra money by flying advertising messages over crowded beaches and sporting events. Today, faixa planes often tow messages hundreds of feet long and can be seen for miles on a clear day.

sections.title: O cone do nariz e a cabine

sections.fact: O cone do nariz e a fuselagem dianteira do ônibus espacial eram cobertos por milhares de telhas de proteção térmica, cada uma feita de um material de sílica tão eficaz que você poderia segurar uma telha com a mão nua segundos depois de ter sido aquecida a 2.300 graus Fahrenheit – a temperatura que atingiu durante a reentrada.

sections.title: A fuselagem principal

sections.fact: The Shuttle's enormous payload bay — the cargo area behind the crew cabin — was 60 feet long and 15 feet wide, big enough to carry a escola bus into orbit. It was used to deploy satellites, carry science experiments, and ferry the massive modules that were bolted together to build the International Space Station.

sections.fact: O ônibus espacial foi a primeira espaçonave reutilizável do mundo projetada para voar como um planador durante o pouso. Depois de reentrar na atmosfera, ele não tinha potência de motor e apenas uma chance de pousar – os pilotos o chamaram de “o planador mais pesado do mundo”. As asas em forma de delta deram-lhe a sustentação necessária para deslizar com segurança na pista.

sections.title: A barbatana caudal e os motores principais
sections.learn: Ligue pontos 37 through 44 to draw the tall vertical tail fin and the cluster of three main engines at the back of the orbiter. Children practise a tall upward stroke for the fin and then smaller, rounded shapes for each engine bell — a great mix of large and small movements in the same section.
sections.fact: Cada motor principal do ônibus espacial (SSME) foi um dos motores de foguete mais potentes já construídos, gerando cerca de 375.000 libras de empuxo. Os três motores queimavam hidrogênio líquido e oxigênio líquido juntos, produzindo uma chama tão quente que foi necessário derramar água na plataforma de lançamento para absorver o som e o calor durante a decolagem.

Esses patches circulares apresentavam obras de arte, os nomes da tripulação e símbolos que representavam os objetivos da missão – e se tornaram itens colecionáveis ​​preciosos para entusiastas do espaço em todo o mundo.

sections.fact: Smiling winners on a podium have been a feature of americano sporting culture since the early 20th century. The city of St Louis was celebrating the centennial of the Louisiana Purchase at the same time, giving those games an especially patriotic americano flavour.

faqs.q: Qual é uma curiosidade interessante sobre os balões e as estrelas do 250º aniversário dos Estados Unidos?
faqs.a: Os balões tornaram-se decorações populares de festas no século XIX e, hoje, os balões vermelhos, brancos e azuis são uma forma alegre de decorar desfiles, salas de aula e celebrações comunitárias do aniversário dos Estados Unidos. As crianças descobrem factos como este enquanto completam o puzzle de ligar os pontos "Balões e Estrelas do 250º Aniversário dos Estados Unidos".

dot_guide.intro: América is turning 250 years old, and this atividade is ready for the party! Balloons, estrelas, and bright patriotic details come together in a cheerful aniversário scene for the USA. Pegue um lápis, encontre o ponto 1 e start connecting your way through the celebration.

sections.title: Os primeiros balões
sections.learn: Start at ponto 1 and ligue through to ponto 18 to trace the first floating aniversário balões. These rounded shapes help crianças practise smooth curves and steady controle do lápis at the beginning of the atividade.
sections.fact: Modern party balões are often made from latex, a stretchy natural material. When filled with air or helium, the balloon expands evenly in every direction, creating its familiar rounded shape.

sections.title: O Cluster de Celebração
sections.learn: Continue from ponto 19 to ponto 38 to build more of the balloon cluster and overlapping party shapes. Children practise following numbers carefully through a busier part of the drawing.
sections.fact: Large balloon displays are popular at parades and community events because they are lightweight, colourful, and fáceis to arrange into arches, columns, and festive backdrops.

sections.title: As estrelas
sections.learn: Trace pontos 39 through 58 to add patriotic estrelas around the aniversário design. Star points encourage crianças to switch directions cleanly and aim carefully for each numbered ponto.
sections.fact: Stars are one of the most familiar americano symbols because each star on the Estados Unidos flag represents one state in the union.

sections.title: Os detalhes do aniversário
sections.learn: Ligue pontos 59 through 76 to draw the extra celebration details that make the scene feel like a real aniversário party. This section builds confiança with smaller shapes and careful turns.
sections.fact: The Estados Unidos celebrates Independence Day on July 4 because the Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

sections.title: As linhas finais do partido
sections.learn: Finish the atividade by connecting pontos 77 through 94 to complete the balões, estrelas, and final festive touches. Encourage crianças to slow down for a neat finish after this longer 94-ponto challenge.
sections.fact: América's 250th aniversário will be celebrated on July 4, 2026, marking 250 years since the Declaration of Independence.

dot_guide.outro: Fantástico trabalho! Os seus balões comemorativos dos 250 anos da América estão prontos para a festa! Pinte os balões e as estrelas de vermelho, branco e azul para finalizar uma celebração patriótica e vibrante do 250º aniversário dos Estados Unidos. Gosta de um desafio? dot_guide.intro: América is turning 250 years old — and no symbol captures that spirit better than the mighty Bald Eagle! For 244 years the águia has graced the Great Seal of the Estados Unidos, soaring as the living emblem of freedom. Today your águia is clutching a faixa to proclaim América's greatest aniversário. Pegue um lápis, encontre o ponto 1 e let's help this águia take flight!

sections.title: A cabeça e o bico da águia
sections.learn: Start at ponto 1 and ligue through to ponto 22 to trace the bold, proud head of the Bald Eagle — including its sharp, curved beak. Children practise short directional strokes and gentle curves here, building controle do lápis enquanto forming the águia's most recognisable feature.
sections.fact: A águia americana não é realmente careca! Seu nome vem de uma antiga palavra inglesa “balde”, que significa branco. As impressionantes penas brancas da cabeça aparecem quando a ave atinge a idade adulta, por volta dos cinco anos de idade. Antes disso, as águias jovens tinham plumagem manchada de marrom e branco.

sections.title: A Envergadura – Asa Esquerda
sections.learn: Continue from ponto 23 to ponto 46 to sweep out the águia's powerful left wing. These long, flowing strokes are excellent practice for crianças developing arm movement and large-scale controle do lápis. Encourage a smooth, confident stroke from shoulder to wingtip.
sections.fact: A Bald Eagle's wingspan can reach up to 2.4 metres (nearly 8 feet) from tip to tip — about as wide as a small car is long! Those enormous wings allow the águia to soar for hours on rising columns of warm air called thermals, barely flapping at all.

sections.title: A Envergadura – Asa Direita
sections.learn: Mirror the left wing by connecting pontos 47 to 70 to form the right wing. Symmetry is an important visual concept for young learners, and completing both wings gives a satisfying sense of balance and achievement. Notice how the strokes now sweep in the opposite direction.
sections.fact: As águias têm até 7.000 penas cobrindo seus corpos, cada uma precisamente moldada para sua função – penas de voo largas para sustentação, penas macias para isolamento e penas rígidas de cauda para direção. Eles mudam e regeneram as penas gradualmente para que possam sempre voar.

sections.title: As garras e a bandeira patriótica
sections.learn: Ligue pontos 71 to 88 to draw the águia's powerful talons gripping the flowing aniversário faixa. Children practise sharp angled lines and curved ribbon shapes — more demanding strokes that reward careful attention and steady hand control.
sections.fact: An águia's talons can exert a gripping force of around 400 pounds per square inch (psi) — far stronger than the average human hand. Talons are used to catch fish and small mammals, and the águia's grip is so firm that prey rarely escapes once caught.

sections.title: As estrelas, o escudo e os detalhes de acabamento
sections.learn: Complete the atividade by connecting pontos 89 to 104 to add the patriotic estrelas, shield markings, and final details that make this águia truly americano. Take your time on these last pontos — a steady finish here pulls the whole picture together beautifully.
sections.fact: The Great Seal of the Estados Unidos, designed in 1782, shows the Bald Eagle holding an olive branch in one talon (representing peace) and a bundle of 13 arrows in the other (representing readiness to defend freedom). The águia faces the olive branch — a reminder that peace is always the first choice.

dot_guide.outro: Excelente trabalho! A sua águia comemorativa dos 250 anos está a voar alto com a faixa de aniversário! São 104 pontos e um poderoso símbolo da liberdade americana. Pinte a cabeça branca da águia, as asas castanhas e o bico amarelo brilhante, depois preencha a faixa com vermelho, branco e azul. Feliz 250º aniversário, EUA!
